question: Does wisdom make people happy?
summary: Proverbs 3:13 says happy (ashre) is the one who finds wisdom and gains understanding. Ecclesiastes 1:18 says in much wisdom is much grief, and increasing knowledge increases sorrow. Two books of the same wisdom canon, opposite conclusions about whether the pursuit of wisdom delivers happiness.

reconcile.connective: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown resolve the tension by confining Ecclesiastes' grief to speculative human inquiry, not to wisdom as such — the sense Proverbs commends.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain wording: Proverbs calls the wisdom-finder happy while Ecclesiastes says increasing wisdom only increases sorrow.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714), on Ecclesiastes 1:12-18
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly and at length, concluding that worldly, speculative learning brings grief while 'he that increases in heavenly wisdom...increases joy,' so Ecclesiastes and Proverbs speak of different kinds of wisdom rather than contradicting each other. (Haley's full text contains no treatment of Ecclesiastes 1:18 or this pairing with Proverbs 3:13; per spec a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage is used instead.)

excerpts.excerpt_text: wisdom . . . knowledge--not in general, for wisdom, &c., are most excellent in their place; but speculative knowledge of man's ways (Ecc 1:13, Ecc 1:17), which, the farther it goes, gives one the more pain to find how "crooked" and "wanting" they are (Ecc 1:15; Ecc 12:12).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles Ecclesiastes' grief-language with Proverbs' 'happy' by restricting Ecc 1:18's complaint to speculative human inquiry into the world's crookedness, not to wisdom in general — the sense Proverbs commends.
